title: Coefficient towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $T$. Work on its small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site]. Powers of ideals and quotient rings have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The ideals $(\ell^n)$ and $(\pi_E^n)$ of $\mathcal O_E$ are cofinal, so we use powers of $\ell$.

For $n\geq1$ put $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and write $q_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$ for the morphism induced by reduction $a\bmod\ell^{n+1}\mapsto a\bmod\ell^n$. The completed coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ is the pullback of the condensed ring of integers as in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Clause (3) of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] identifies it with the uniformizer-power inverse limit for every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. For finite subextensions of the fixed algebraic closure this is also the first comparison of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Using the cofinal powers of $\ell$ gives
$$\mathcal O_{E,T}\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_n.$$
The inverse limit is a limit of sheaves of rings, computed sectionwise [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. In this definition the notation $\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$ means $R_n$.

Define $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ as follows. An object is a system $C_\bullet=(C_n,t_n)_{n\geq1}$, where $C_n$ is a sheaf of $R_n$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $t_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ is a morphism of sheaves of abelian groups satisfying, on every site object $U$,
$$t_{n,U}(a x)=q_{n,U}(a)t_{n,U}(x)\quad(a\in R_{n+1}(U),\ x\in C_{n+1}(U)).$$
Equivalently, $t_n$ is an $R_{n+1}$-linear map $C_{n+1}\to(q_n)_*C_n$, where $(q_n)_*$ denotes restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The underlying sheaves and transitions form an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system]. A morphism $\varphi:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet=(D_n,s_n)$ is a family of $R_n$-linear sheaf maps $\varphi_n:C_n\to D_n$ with
$$s_n\circ\varphi_{n+1}=\varphi_n\circ t_n\quad(n\geq1).$$
Identities and composition are componentwise. We write $\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^\bullet=(R_n,q_n)_{n\geq1}$ for the tower of coefficient rings.
